x: Only the Python runtime actually executes: the handler's source runs in a sandboxed interpreter (curated builtins, a stdlib allow-list, no filesystem/network/process access). Node.js/.NET/Java/Ruby runtimes can be selected and stored, but Invoke always runs the stored source as Python.
Weighted alias routing is stored and returned exactly as configured, but Invoke always runs $LATEST/the alias's primary version — Vyomi does not probabilistically split traffic.
A layer's content is stored and sized for real, but it is never merged into the sandbox at Invoke time — attaching a layer records the association without changing what the function can import.

Creating, listing, enabling/disabling and deleting a trigger (SQS, DynamoDB, Kinesis, S3, SNS, EventBridge, API Gateway, CloudWatch Logs) is real and stateful. An SQS-sourced trigger really invokes the function the instant a message is sent (see sqs.lambda-triggers); the other source types have no poller/subscriber behind them, so those triggers never invoke the function on their own — LastProcessingResult stays "No records processed" for them. A direct Invoke (Test tab or the native API) always runs code regardless of source type.

Setting ReservedConcurrentExecutions to 0 really throttles — every Invoke is rejected with TooManyRequestsException and Throttles increments, exactly as real Lambda does. A positive reservation is stored and returned, but never enforced against concurrent callers — Vyomi runs every Invoke synchronously (nothing to run concurrently), so no invoke is ever rejected for exceeding a nonzero reservation.

On a real async (Event) Invoke, the OnSuccess/OnFailure destination (SQS queue, SNS topic or another Lambda function) really receives the invocation envelope, and a legacy DeadLetterConfig really receives the raw event on failure when no OnFailure destination is set — same precedence and envelope shape as real Lambda. An EventBridge event-bus destination is accepted and stored but never delivered to (counts toward AsyncDeliveryFailures) — Vyomi's cross-core delivery seam only reaches SQS/SNS/Lambda targets.

features.t: VPC config and EFS file systems
x: SubnetIds/SecurityGroupIds are validated for real: both must be given together (or both omitted, to detach), and each ID must look like a real EC2 resource ID — a malformed or missing pair is rejected with InvalidParameterValueException, exactly as real Lambda rejects it at Create/UpdateFunctionConfiguration time. An EFS access point's Arn and LocalMountPath are format-validated the same way. Vyomi has no shared VPC engine on this seam, so a syntactically valid but nonexistent subnet, security group or file system is still accepted; once a config passes validation it is stored and returned exactly as configured — Vyomi never attaches a real ENI or mounts a real file system, so code never actually reaches the VPC or the file system at Invoke time.

features.t: Monitor tab metrics and recent invocations
x: Invocations/Duration/Error metrics and the recent-invocations list are real — computed from the function's actual last 20 Invoke calls — but this is Vyomi's own lightweight read, not a real CloudWatch Logs Insights / X-Ray integration. Throttles and AsyncDeliveryFailures are real running counters (see lambda.concurrency / lambda.destinations); ConcurrentExecutions always reads 0 — Vyomi never runs two invocations of a function at once.

A function's attached code signing config really gates CreateFunction/UpdateFunctionCode: with the config's validation policy set to Enforce, a deploy is rejected with CodeVerificationFailedException unless it declares a SigningProfileVersionArn that is one of the config's AllowedPublishers; with Warn, an unsigned/untrusted deploy is still allowed, exactly like real Lambda. Vyomi has no AWS Signer integration or cryptographic signature pipeline, so 'signed' means the deploy call declares a trusted signing profile ARN — there is no real signature to forge or verify over the code bytes themselves.

features.t: Code signing configurations (create, list, update, delete)
x: The configuration resource (allowed signing profiles, validation policy) is stored and returned for real, and is enforced against deployments of any function it is attached to (see lambda.code-signing). A code signing config cannot be deleted while still attached to a function — Vyomi rejects that with ResourceConflictException, matching real Lambda.

The capacity provider resource (name, architectures, max vCPU, scaling mode, VPC) is stored and returned for real. It never actually schedules a function onto reserved EC2 instances — Vyomi's Lambda core only has one runtime, the sandboxed serverless one; attaching a capacity provider doesn't change where Invoke runs.

The connector resource (VPC, protocol, compute type) is stored and returned for real. It never actually bridges network traffic — there is no MicroVM runtime on the other end of the connection (see lambda.microvms).

MicroVM images and running MicroVMs are stored and returned for real (name, state, version, status). There is no Firecracker runtime underneath — a MicroVM never actually boots or runs code; it is a tracked resource record only.

An application is a tracked deployment record (name, description, status, template) stored and returned for real. Vyomi has no CloudFormation/SAM core, so creating one never actually provisions the underlying Lambda functions, APIs or tables a template would describe — Status always reads CREATE_COMPLETE immediately.

A replica record is derived directly from the function it replicates (same Description/Runtime/LastModified) and the region list is stored for real. Vyomi has no CloudFront distribution to deploy a replica to, so a replica is never actually invoked at an edge location — the record is bookkeeping only.

Not a Lambda resource — this page lists real Step Functions state machines (core/stepfunctions_core.py) for the console cross-link real AWS Lambda shows; create/execute them for real in the Step Functions console.

features.t: Step Functions state machines using a function
x: Derived live from the real Step Functions core: ListStateMachines + DescribeStateMachine, filtered to definitions that reference the function ARN or name.

The helper creates a real RDS Proxy record in the function's own subnets and security groups (CreateDBProxy with the Secrets Manager auth + IAM role, RegisterDBProxyTargets with an engine-family check) and lists the proxies in the function's VPC with their targets. Vyomi does not proxy connections (apps still connect to the instance endpoint), does not rewrite the function's IAM role (no rds-db:connect policy is attached) and proxy endpoints are labels, not resolvable hosts.

features.t: AI coding-agent onboarding (MCP gateway + agent prompt)
x: Real: checks the local model, creates an AgentCore MCP gateway that exposes Lambda functions as tools, and generates the endpoint configuration prompt. There is no hosted coding agent; the agent that uses the prompt is your own.

Real Source -> Build -> Deploy pipeline (core/lambda_cicd_core.py): the repository (vyomi/<name>, seeded with a working function, or a GitHub repo fetched with the user's own PAT on the offline appliance) is validated and packaged (handler module must exist, every .py must compile), then the function is created or its code updated through the real Lambda core, a version is published and the 'live' alias moved - the deployed function is invocable with the pushed code. A push to a vyomi/ repository (POST .../pipeline/push, or a git push to Gitea on offline) starts an execution; GitHub does not call back, so 'Release change' starts one.

The drag-and-drop canvas is real and deploys through the real service APIs: a CloudFormation stack for SQS/SNS/S3/DynamoDB resources, CreateFunction for Lambda functions (default python handler code), CreateEventSourceMapping for SQS -> function and SNS Subscribe for SNS -> function. It authors plain CloudFormation, not a SAM (AWS::Serverless) template: no API Gateway, Step Functions, layers or per-function code editing on the canvas. S3/DynamoDB nodes are deployed but cannot be wired to a function.
